 San Miguel Beermen, Ginebra duke it out in Governors’ Cup quarterfinals 
 A “BEERACLE” type reverse sweep or a closeout that’s just delayed? 
 November 9, 2026 | 7:29 pm 
 SAN MIGUEL BEERMEN 
vs Barangay Ginebra — PBA.PH 
 Game on Tuesday 
 (Ynares Center Antipolo) 
 7:30 p.m. – Ginebra vs San Miguel (Game 5) 
 *Series tied, 2-2 
 A “BEERACLE” type reverse sweep or a closeout that’s just delayed?
 San Miguel Beermen (SMB) — out for an amazing comeback from 0-2 down — and Barangay Ginebra — bent on claiming the clincher on third try — duke it out in a Game 5 sudden death in the PBA Governors’ Cup quarterfinals. 
 The moment of reckoning is set at 7:30 p.m. at Ynares Center Antipolo.
 Reward for the victor is a date with defending champion TNT in the best-of-five semifinals.
 It’s been a fierce series between the two proud and glory-hungry franchises from the San Miguel Corp. group.
 Reigning Commissioner’s Cup kingpin Ginebra opened with emphatic 104-95 and 126-99 victories to get on the hill early. But current Philippine Cup titlist SMB struck back twice, 101-99 and 108-102, to forge the rubber match. 
 PBA aficionados are quick to point to the possibility of a repeat of San Miguel’s celebrated “beeracle” feat in the 2015-16 Philippine Cup finals against Alaska. In that best-of-seven series, the Beermen went down 0-3 but famously fought their way back to complete the monumental steal.
 Coach Leo Austria and his troops led by June Mar Fajardo and Chris Ross, two holdovers from that legendary comeback win, shrugged off the “beeracle” label.
 “We will not exaggerate the situation. We just have to play our game and we just want to focus on what we have to do (in Game 5), ” said Mr. Austria.
 “We haven’t done anything yet. We just evened the series. They won two straight, we won two straight. It’s a decider and it’s usually how it goes when we play Ginebra. We go six or seven (games in a best-of-seven) so we’re excited to play that next game,” said Mr. Ross.
 Ginebra’s situation is still salvageable. And that’s what matters to coach Tim Cone at this point.
 “Bottom line is, it’s tied up, 2-2. We move forward, all right, get ready for the next one,” said Mr. Cone after the Game 4 heartbreaker. 
 If SMB has a history of great comebacks, Mr. Cone has a prior bad experience of going two-nil only to concede the last three matches of a race-to-three himself. That happened when Mr. Cone’s Alaska fell to Purefoods in five in the finals of the 1990 PBA Third Conference.
 And now, his troops led by Scottie Thompson and Jordan Murphy would do everything in their power to prevent another botched job. — Olmin Leyba
